title: 4. Machine Learning Process & Pipeline
description: Master the 5-step iterative machine learning lifecycle.

blocks.content:
### The 5-Step ML Pipeline

Building ML applications follows a structured end-to-end pipeline rather than a single coding step:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Step1["1. Data Collection & Cleaning"] --> Step2["2. Data Preprocessing"]
    Step2 --> Step3["3. Feature Engineering"]
    Step3 --> Step4["4. Model Training"]
    Step4 --> Step5["5. Evaluation & Tuning"]
    Step5 -.->|"Iterate & Refine"| Step3
```

1. **Data Collection & Cleaning**: Remove duplicate rows, fix corrupted formats.
2. **Data Preprocessing**: Handle missing values, scale numbers, encode text.
3. **Feature Engineering**: Select or construct features with strong predictive power.
4. **Model Training**: Train algorithm options on training data.
5. **Evaluation & Fine-Tuning**: Measure validation performance and iterate.

> **Golden Rule**: Garbage in, garbage out! Improving data quality almost always yields bigger gains than picking a more complex model algorithm.

A useful ML project is a loop: define the question, collect examples, prepare them, train, test, and improve. The model is only one step in the loop.

Start with a clear success measure. “Make a good model” is vague; “catch spam without hiding normal mail” is a testable goal.

blocks.question: If your machine learning model performs poorly on validation tests, what is often the most effective next step?
options: Delete all the data and stop
Go back and improve data cleaning, missing value handling, and feature engineering
Increase the font size in your code editor
Switch immediately to deep learning without checking the data
blocks.explanation: Machine learning is iterative; refining data preprocessing and features usually resolves performance issues.
